text:
Incident Bot: Paging: high p95 latency on embeddings-service in us-west-2 — >2s for 12m, paging policy fired. Link: https://ops.redwood.example/incidents/1978501234 :rotating_light:
Jordan (oncall): saw it, I'm on it. starting live triage.
Aisha - SRE: adding context — last deploy 03/12 22:10 UTC to runtime-3, CPU stable but GPUs showing long tail.
Jordan (oncall): initial mitigation — temporarily disable cross-region reroutes to reduce fanout, will measure.
Priya - EngRuntime: noted. rolling back a small config change from the deploy that touched kv-cache expiry? I can look.
Lina - Observability: creating a short dashboard so we can watch p50/p95/p99 and per-model tail. pinned here: https://dashboards.redwood.example/d/abcd/embedding-latency-live
Garret - Product: customer-impact check — any errors or just slow tokens? Getting reports from a single enterprise tenant about timeouts at their client.
Jordan (oncall): mostly slow responses, some client timeouts at 30s. Paging escalation intact. I set a temporary alert mute for that tenant to avoid duplicate pages while we triage (:eyes:), will not affect global paging.
Aisha - SRE: hypothesis — KV cache misses spiking; the runtime shows cache eviction rate x6. If that’s the case, increasing cache retention or disabling an aggressive prefetch could help.
Priya - EngRuntime: found the config diff — an autoscaler flag accidentally lowered KV cache size on new instances. Reverting now.
Incident Bot: Config revert applied by Priya - EngRuntime at 1978501470.
Jordan (oncall): after revert, p95 trending down from 2.3s -> 1.1s over 5m. continuing to monitor. recommend we adjust alerting to avoid a pager for short transient cache-pressure spikes.
Lina - Observability: proposal — change alert from p95 > 1.5s sustained 10m to p95 > 2.0s sustained 5m OR p99 > 2.5s sustained 5m; also add a new dashboard panel for per-tenant timeout counts.
Garret - Product: agree on lowering noise, but we need a signal for customer-facing timeouts. add a synthetic check that simulates the enterprise tenant path.
Jordan (oncall): assigning follow-ups — Priya to open runtime PR to revert accidental config and add a guard, Aisha to update runbook section "embedding-service cache pressure" with rollback steps and links, Lina to add dashboard panel + create alert playbook note. I'll shepherd the alert threshold change in alerting config after we land PR.
Priya - EngRuntime: will open PR now: https://git.redwood.example/runtime/pull/582 — includes revert + unit tests.
Aisha - SRE: runbook note draft: `https://confluence.redwood.example/runbooks/embedding-cache-pressure` — will annotate with incident timeline and add the alert ownership field (oncall -> eng-runtime).
Lina - Observability: updated dashboard panel and added alert annotation. New alert rule id: EMB-LAT-1978. I left the old rule in place but squelched pages to critical only for 1h.
Jordan (oncall): monitoring looks stable. closing the paging incident in 15m if no regressions. post-incident: we'll push the alert tuning + runbook edits to staging and coordinate sign-off from eng-runtime + SRE.
Garret - Product: pls add the synthetic tenant check to the QA suite so we catch this early.
Priya - EngRuntime: noted, will add synthetic test in the PR and link it in the runbook.
Jordan (oncall): action items summary (I'll paste into follow-up): 1) runtime PR (Priya) 2) runbook update (Aisha) 3) dashboard + alert rule change (Lina) 4) synthetic check (Priya + Garret) 5) postmortem note w/ customer impact and timeline (Jordan). Assigning owners in the follow-up doc.
Incident Bot: Incident acknowledged resolved (paging cleared) at 1978501899.
Jordan (oncall): thanks all — great quick coordination. please update the runbook links in the follow-up doc before EOD. :thumbsup:
